seoTitle: Merge Cells in Smartsheet: The Real Alternatives
metaDescription: Smartsheet doesn't support traditional cell merging like Excel, but parent-child hierarchies and JOIN formulas achieve the same visual grouping.
intro: If you're coming from Excel, you might go looking for a merge cells button in Smartsheet and not find one. That's intentional, since Smartsheet's grid structure avoids the row-breaking issues traditional merging can cause. This guide covers the native alternatives that get you the same visual effect.

steps.heading: Understand why merging is omitted
steps.body: Smartsheet's grid structure avoids traditional multi-column cell merging to prevent broken rows and dataset corruption.

steps.heading: Use Parent-Child Row Hierarchies
steps.body: Group rows underneath a single spanning header row to create a visual structure similar to a merged cell.

steps.heading: Style parent rows for emphasis
steps.body: Apply background fills, bold fonts, and borders to parent rows to make the grouped structure clearly scannable.

steps.heading: Combine text with JOIN
steps.body: Use the JOIN function or the + operator to combine text from separate columns into a single cell.

steps.heading: Set up rollups for numbers
steps.body: Configure parent-row rollup formulas to automatically summarize or combine numeric values from child rows.

faq.question: Does Smartsheet have a merge cells button like Excel?
faq.answer: No, Smartsheet intentionally omits traditional cell merging to protect grid structure and prevent broken rows.

faq.question: How do I get a visual effect similar to merged cells?
faq.answer: Using Parent-Child Row Hierarchies to group rows under a spanning header row achieves a similar visual result.

faq.question: Can I combine text from two columns into one?
faq.answer: Yes, the JOIN function or the + operator lets you combine text from separate columns into a single cell.

faq.question: Will collapsing rows help clean up a grouped structure?
faq.answer: Yes, expanding and collapsing grouped subtasks beneath parent categories helps manage large boards without visual clutter.
